title: How are the lengths of a line's three views related?
description: A line goes some distance along, some deep and some up. The board finds the length of its front, top and side views, compares each with the line, and adds their squares. The relation is that no view is longer than the line and the three squares add up to twice the square of the line.
teaching_notes: One idea: each view keeps two of the three directions of the line, so its square is the sum of two of the three squares. Watch for students who think a view can be longer than the line.

source: Figure it Out (views of solids, question 1)
video_script.why: The child relates the lengths of the three views of a line by looking from each direction as for the cylinder, because each view keeps two of the line's three directions.
video_script.substitution: line goes a along, b deep, c up; front view squared = a x a + c x c; top view squared = a x a + b x b; side view squared = b x b + c x c; line squared = a x a + b x b + c x c; sum of the three squares = 2 x (a x a + b x b + c x c) = 2 x line squared.
video_script.anchor: a slanted line in a box with its front, top and side views drawn as three lines on the three walls
video_script.payoff_line: No view is longer than the line. The squares of the three view lengths add up to twice the square of the line's length

final_answer.value: No view is longer than the line; the squares of the three view lengths add up to twice the square of the line's length
final_answer.spoken: no view is longer than the line; the squares of the three view lengths add up to twice the square of the line's length

hold_back: No view is longer than the line; the squares of the three view lengths add up to twice the square of the line's length
maths_rules: the front view keeps along and up, the top view keeps along and deep, the side view keeps deep and up
front view squared = a x a + c x c; top view squared = a x a + b x b; side view squared = b x b + c x c
the top view lies flat and the line rises c above its end, a right triangle: line squared = a x a + b x b + c x c
each view square is the line square with one of the three squares missing, so no view is longer than the line
a view is as long as the line only when the missing direction is 0, that is, when the line is parallel to that plane
sum of the three view squares = 2 x (a x a + b x b + c x c) = 2 x line squared
check: a line running only along has front view and top view equal to the line and a side view of length 0; line squared + line squared + 0 = 2 x line squared
video_script.design: One idea: the method of the worked cylinder, applied to a line. The line sits in a box on the stage and its three views appear on the three walls; each view is written as the sum of two squares in its own colour.

<bookmark mark='line'/>The line goes along, deep and up inside a box.

<bookmark mark='walls'/>Here are the front view, the top view and the side view of the line.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is there any relation between their lengths?

beats.on_screen: Given: a line that goes a along, b deep and c up

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how the lengths of the three views are related.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: front view squared = a x a + c x c; top view squared = a x a + b x b; side view squared = b x b + c x c

marks.front: the front view is drawn as the longest side of a right triangle with sides a and c
marks.top: the top view is drawn as the longest side of a right triangle with sides a and b
marks.side: the side view is drawn as the longest side of a right triangle with sides b and c

narration: <bookmark mark='front'/>Step one, find the length of each view. The front view keeps along and up, so its square is along squared plus up squared.
<bookmark mark='top'/>The top view keeps along and deep, so its square is along squared plus deep squared.
<bookmark mark='side'/>The side view keeps deep and up, so its square is deep squared plus up squared.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the top view lies flat and the line rises c above its end; line squared = (a x a + b x b) + c x c

marks.tri: the line, its top view and the rise c are drawn as a right triangle
marks.sum: the working line squared = a x a + b x b + c x c is written

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step two, find the line's own length. The top view lies flat, and the line rises up from its end. They make a right triangle.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The square of the line is the square of the top view plus up squared. That is along squared plus deep squared plus up squared.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: each view squared is the line squared with one square missing, so each view is at most as long as the line

marks.miss: in each view, one of the three squares is crossed out
marks.equal: a view equals the line only when the crossed out direction is 0, with the line parallel to that plane

narration: <bookmark mark='miss'/>Step three, compare each view with the line. Each view square has one of the three squares missing, so no view is longer than the line.
<bookmark mark='equal'/>A view is as long as the line only when the missing direction is zero. That is when the line is parallel to that plane.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: (a x a + c x c) + (a x a + b x b) + (b x b + c x c) = 2 x (a x a + b x b + c x c) = 2 x line squared

marks.add: the three view squares are added
marks.twice: each of the three squares appears twice, so the total is written as 2 times the line squared

beats.colours: three colours, one for each view
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step four, add the squares of the three views.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>Along squared, deep squared and up squared each appear twice. The total is twice the line's square.

beats.on_screen: Check: a line that runs only along: front view and top view equal the line, side view is a dot; line squared + line squared + 0 = 2 x line squared

marks.flat: a line lying flat and running only along is drawn in the box
marks.dot: its front view and top view are as long as the line and its side view is a dot
marks.total: the three squares are added to line squared + line squared + 0

narration: <bookmark mark='flat'/>Step five, check with a line that runs only along.
<bookmark mark='dot'/>Its front view and top view are as long as the line. Its side view is a dot.
<bookmark mark='total'/>The squares add up to the line's square, twice over, and nothing more. The rule holds.

beats.on_screen: Answer: No view is longer than the line; the squares of the three view lengths add up to twice the square of the line's length
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>No view is longer than the line. The squares of the three view lengths add up to twice the square of the line's length.
